detail.longDescription: It has been suggested that I should use PyMySQL as opposed to mysql-connector-python as it is apparently faster and more reliable. However I cannot find any information on how to close a PyMySQL pool cleanly. Do they even need closing manually or does it close the idle connections itself as it is removed from memory? import pymysql.cursors import pymysqlpool config={'host':'...', 'database':'...', 'user':'...', 'password':'...', 'autocommit':True} db_pool = pymysqlpool.ConnectionPool(size=2, maxsize=3, pre_create_num=2, name='db_pool', **config) db_conn = db_pool.get_connection() # ... run pymysql db_conn.close() # <- this closes active connection db_pool = None # <- how to close all idle connections cleanly
